audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text puts the poke in the wrong stance: "his ranged Q poke in Hammer stance and the Acceleration Gate + Q shock-blast burst".
audit.why: Riot's text splits the Q explicitly — "Hammer Stance: Leaps to an enemy dealing physical damage and slowing enemies. Cannon Stance: Fires an orb of electricity...". The ranged poke is Cannon stance (Shock Blast); the Hammer Q is a melee leap. A Zac player told the ranged poke comes from Hammer stance will read the wrong weapon glow and mistime every walk-up.
audit.corrected: Shock Blast is the Cannon-stance Q; the Hammer Q is a melee leap.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mercury Cannon's resistance reduction appears nowhere, in an entry whose advice is "Build a little armor" and "out-sustain".
audit.why: Riot's text: in Cannon Stance the transform means "The first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist." Against a Zac who is buying resistances every recall, a free Armor AND MR cut on the first attack after every swap is the single most relevant thing his ultimate does, and it argues for health and sustain over stacking resistances alone.
audit.corrected: His Cannon-form first attack cuts both your Armor and your MR — resistances alone are not the plan.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hextech Capacitor is never mentioned; the only escape tool named is "Gate speed".
audit.why: Riot's text: "When Jayce swaps weapons he gains Move Speed for a short duration." The swap itself is on a 6s cooldown, so the speed burst is repeatable roughly every six seconds — that, not just the Acceleration Gate, is why he is hard to stick to after a poke. It changes how a Zac player plans a chase.
audit.corrected: Every stance swap gives him a Move Speed burst, and the swap is on 6s.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers in either layer; breakdown.cooldowns reads "matchup-defining — His main poke. Dodge it."
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 and only reaches 6s at rank 6, and Thundering Blow is 20s at rank 1. Those are long enough to count and they define opposite things: the first is how long Zac is safe to walk up, the second is how long his engage goes unanswered once the knockback is spent.
audit.corrected: Shock Blast 16s at rank 1 falling to 6s; Thundering Blow 20s at rank 1; your Slingshot 21s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1] is titled "Build a little armor".
audit.why: Jayce's damage is split by stance: Shock Blast deals physical damage, Thundering Blow deals magic damage, and the Hammer-form first attack after a swap adds bonus magic. Armour alone reads only half of it.
audit.corrected: Armour plus some MR — his Q is physical and his E is magic.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart gives Jayce 6 of 7 stages at a 51.48% Zac win rate over 237 games, while the full layer reads Jayce / Skill / Zac / Zac / Jayce / Zac / Zac. No defect was flagged for this entry, but the two layers still disagree and the content one disagrees with the data.
audit.why: The full layer's split is the one consistent with 51.48% and with the mechanics: Jayce owns level 1 outright on range, and level 6 is his because of the resistance cut, but once Zac has Elastic Slingshot the 20s Thundering Blow becomes the whole question, and his blob sustain plus a flat 5s W out-last poke he has to land repeatedly.
audit.corrected: Jayce / Skill / Zac / Zac / Jayce / Zac / Zac.

notes:
CAUTION for whoever writes Jayce content next: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json lists ONE cooldown line per slot (e.g. E = "20/18/16/14/12/10") because Data Dragon stores one spell object per slot, even though each slot is two different abilities in two stances. Do not read that as the two stances sharing a cooldown — Jayce combos cast Cannon Q and Hammer Q back to back, so they cannot share one. I nearly wrote a decisive-sounding line ("if he gates a Shock Blast he cannot knock you back") on that basis and dropped it. The per-rank numbers themselves are fine to quote; the shared-cooldown inference is not.

Left alone deliberately: the repeated claim that Thundering Blow's knockback "cancels your Slingshot" (mid, whys[2], spikes[1], wants.foe[1]). A knockback is a displacement and plausibly does interrupt Zac's E, but nothing in the kit files establishes it, so I neither repeated it as fact in new text nor contradicted it. Worth a League Wiki check.

phases[i].side and diff/diffRating cannot be proposed (full-layer "before" must be at least 12 characters), so the full layer keeps TRICKY 7.5/10 while the content win[] chart is brought into line with the win rate.

WKM_LINES ERROR (champion-level, champ-data/what-kills-me.js, jayce line 2): "Hammer-form Q knockback into full melee combo is the all-in". The knockback is Hammer E (Thundering Blow) — Riot: "Deals magic damage to an enemy and knocks them back." Hammer Q (To the Skies!) is a leap that damages and slows, with no knockback. Same line calls form swaps "cooldown resets", which is also loose: the two stances hold independent cooldowns, the swap does not refresh them.
